themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints exploded to 8 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike—signaling either a sudden service collapse or emerging sanitation crisis in Flatbush/PLG neighborhoods.
evidence: 8 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.29)
Convergence with other sanitation signals: Dirty Condition (418 complaints over 90 days) and Unsanitary Condition (704 complaints over 90 days) remain elevated baseline concerns
No recent Sanitation Department service announcements or workforce changes identified in available data
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about staffing levels, equipment availability, or schedule changes in CD 309 this week
Survey residents on specific blocks with complaints to document which neighborhoods are most affected
Track whether this is a one-week anomaly or the start of a sustained trend by monitoring next week's data

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge Downtown
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 22 last week, up 577% from the 8-week average of 3.2 per week, suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or a breakdown in removal services across Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (577% spike, z-score: 6.19)
Convergence with street light complaints (14 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 167%), suggesting broader public realm maintenance concerns
No Reddit discussions or recent local news coverage of graffiti activity in the district
reporting_angles: Map the 22 complaints to identify geographic clusters—are specific neighborhoods or corridors being targeted?
Interview Parks/Sanitation about removal capacity and response times; determine if this is gang-related or copycat activity
Document before/after photos of heavily tagged areas to illustrate scale and visibility

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Alert
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 last week, up 700% from a baseline of 0.4 per week over 8 weeks, indicating a potential foodborne illness cluster or contamination event requiring immediate public health investigation.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Recent local coverage mentions 'A Caribbean Burger Spot Finds Success' (Documented, 2026-03-30), but no health violations reported
No DOHMH public health advisories identified in available data; timing warrants urgent verification
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health immediately to identify which restaurants/food vendors generated the 3 complaints and their inspection status
Determine if complaints cluster around a single establishment or are dispersed across multiple vendors
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timeline, and which establishments they patronized to narrow etiology

themes_detail.label: Water System Strain
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 38 two weeks ago, up 354% from the 8-week average of 8.4 per week, alongside elevated water leak and plumbing complaints (456 and 614 respectively over 90 days), suggesting infrastructure stress or potential contamination event.
evidence: 38 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (354% spike, z-score: 5.53)
Water leak complaints: 456 over 90 days; plumbing complaints: 614 over 90 days—both in top 10 complaint categories
Heat/hot water complaints dominate (3,885 over 90 days), many linked to water system failures; potential convergence signal
reporting_angles: Request DEP data on main breaks, pressure loss events, or boil water advisories in CD 309 around the spike 2 weeks ago
Investigate whether the spike correlates with seasonal demand, aging infrastructure, or a specific incident (main break, contamination)
Interview residents about water quality, pressure, temperature issues to assess ongoing impact beyond the initial spike

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints hit 10 three weeks ago, up 1043% from the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week, the single largest percentage spike in the dataset, suggesting either a remediation project revealing contamination or a broader building safety concern.
evidence: 10 asbestos complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1043% spike, z-score: 8.66—highest z-score in dataset)
346 building permits filed in last 90 days (197 alterations, 93 new buildings, 6 demolitions), many potentially triggering asbestos disclosure/remediation
Heat/hot water and plumbing complaints remain elevated, potentially linked to remediation work disrupting utilities
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings generated the 10 asbestos complaints via DOB and CEQR records; determine if they share a common contractor or builder
Interview residents in affected buildings about relocation, health impacts, remediation timelines, and tenant protections
Investigate whether complaints are tied to renovation projects or emergency demolitions; assess if adequate community notice was provided
